page: Amazon Web Services i3.xlarge is a storage-optimized instance utilizing the Xen hypervisor and x86_64 architecture. It is equipped with an Intel Xeon E5-2686 v4 processor running at 2.3 GHz, delivering 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores with hyper-threading. The hardware configuration includes 30.0 GB of system memory and a bundled 950 GB local NVMe SSD. Network connectivity is rated at a baseline bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate that the instance operates in the lower tiers for compute and memory subsystems. Single-core and multi-core CPU tests, including stress-ng and Geekbench, place the processor in the bottom 10% of tested servers. Memory bandwidth is similarly constrained, with uncached read and write speeds registering in the bottom 10% to 25%. Database operations, such as Redis SET and Passmark database tests, also fall into the bottom 25% tier.

Qualitatively, the i3.xlarge provides a high density of local NVMe storage and memory relative to its compute resources, making it cost-effective for workloads that require local storage capacity without demanding high-performance CPU throughput. This profile makes the instance suitable for legacy storage-intensive applications, NoSQL databases, transactional data stores, and basic web serving where local NVMe caching is beneficial.
description: Amazon Web Services i3.xlarge is a storage-optimized instance featuring an Intel Xeon E5-2686 v4 processor with 4 dedicated vCPUs, 2 physical cores, and 30.0 GB of RAM. Operating on the Xen hypervisor with an x86_64 architecture, it includes a bundled 950 GB local NVMe SSD and a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps. Benchmark evaluations place its compute and memory performance in the bottom 10% to 25% tiers, indicating limitations in raw processing power and memory bandwidth. However, the instance offers qualitative cost efficiency for storage-centric workloads that prioritize local NVMe capacity over high CPU performance. The platform's dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent, albeit modest, execution speeds for legacy enterprise applications. It is best suited for NoSQL databases, transactional data stores, and local caching applications that benefit from high-capacity local storage.
